items.informal_name: Partial Derivative Correspondence under Bivariate-Multivariate Polynomial Isomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : Polynomial (Polynomial R)),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv 1) ((Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial R) p) =
    (Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial R) (Polynomial.derivative p)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and polynomial $ p $ in the bivariate polynomial ring $ R[X][Y] $, the partial derivative of $ p $ with respect to the second variable $ Y $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[X_0, X_1] $ (via the canonical isomorphism) equals the derivative of $ p $ with respect to $ Y $ in the bivariate ring, converted through the same isomorphism. Formally, $ \frac{\partial}{\partial X_1} \left( \text{equiv}(p) \right) = \text{equiv} \left( \frac{d}{dY} p \right) $, where $ \text{equiv} $ denotes the bivariate-to-multivariate polynomial isomorphism.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative Correspondence in Bivariate and Multivariate Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : Polynomial (Polynomial R)),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv 1) ((Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial R) p) =
    (Polynomial.Bivariate.equivMvPolynomial R) (Polynomial.derivative p)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in the bivariate polynomial ring $ R[X][Y] $, the partial derivative of $ p $ with respect to the second variable $ Y $ corresponds under the canonical isomorphism $ \phi: R[X][Y] \to R[X_0, X_1] $ to the partial derivative of $ \phi(p) $ with respect to the second variable $ X_1 $. Specifically, $ \phi(\partial_Y p) = \partial_{X_1} \phi(p) $, where $ \partial_Y $ denotes differentiation in the bivariate ring and $ \partial_{X_1} $ denotes differentiation in the multivariate ring.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order 1 Equals Standard Derivative
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (f : Polynomial R), (Polynomial.hasseDeriv 1) f = Polynomial.derivative f
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order 1 applied to $ f $ coincides with the standard derivative of $ f $. Specifically, $ D^{(1)}(f) = f' $, where $ D^{(1)} $ denotes the first Hasse derivative and $ f' $ denotes the usual derivative in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $.

This equivalence maps polynomials in $ R[X][Y] $ to multivariate polynomials by interpreting $ X $ and $ Y $ as distinct variables $ X_0 $ and $ X_1 $, and vice versa, with compositions of evaluations proving bijectivity.

items.informal_name: Derivative Preservation under Algebra Equivalence for Separable Elements
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Differential A] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommRing R]
  [inst_3 : Differential R] [inst_4 : Algebra A R] [DifferentialAlgebra A R] {R' : Type u_3} [inst_6 : CommRing R']
  [inst_7 : Differential R'] [inst_8 : Algebra A R'] [DifferentialAlgebra A R'] [IsDomain R'] (f : R ≃ₐ[A] R') (x : R),
  IsSeparable A x → f x′ = (f x)′
items.informal_description: For an $ A $-algebra equivalence $ f : R \to R' $ and a separable element $ x \in R $ over $ A $, it holds that $ f(x') = (f(x))' $, where $ x' $ denotes the derivative of $ x $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence of Polynomial Rings Induced by Coefficient Mapping
items.type:
{R : Type u} →
  {A : Type z} →
    {B : Type u_2} →
      [inst : CommSemiring R] →
        [inst_1 : Semiring A] →
          [inst_2 : Semiring B] →
            [inst_3 : Algebra R A] → [inst_4 : Algebra R B] → (A ≃ₐ[R] B) → Polynomial A ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial B
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and $ R $-algebras $ A $ and $ B $, if there exists an $ R $-algebra equivalence $ f : A ≃ₐ[R] B $, then the induced $ R $-algebra homomorphism from the polynomial ring $ A[X] $ to $ B[X] $ defined by applying $ f $ coefficient-wise is itself an algebra equivalence. This means the map $ \text{Polynomial.mapAlgHom}(f) : A[X] → B[X] $ is invertible, with inverse given by $ \text{Polynomial.mapAlgHom}(f^{-1}) $, establishing an isomorphism between the polynomial rings that preserves both ring operations and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $.

items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and $ R $-algebras $ A $ and $ B $, if there exists an $ R $-algebra equivalence $ f : A ≃ₐ[R] B $, then the induced map $ A[X] → B[X] $ defined by applying $ f $ coefficient-wise is an $ R $-algebra equivalence.
